research_question: Can a standalone radar/WSST beat-anchor localization head learn accurate beat positions, and does better anchor quality raise continuous ECG assembly PCC toward the oracle ceiling?
hypothesis: Training AnchorHeatmapNet on fold_01 pushes anchor F1@100ms from the ~0.3 predicted-anchor baseline toward 0.7-0.8, and predicted-anchor OLA PCC (morphology given) rises toward the oracle ceiling (~0.93-0.98).
protocol: Fold-01 strict LOSO, WSST input, standalone anchor localization only (no waveform decoder).
baseline: Predicted-anchor assembly from prior REM R-mask (q1_align_ceval_pred_anchor_fold01): anchor-driven PCC 0.23-0.37; oracle ceiling 0.93-0.96.
changed_variable: Dedicated anchor localization head + CenterNet focal loss on Gaussian R heatmap, trained as an independent task.
controlled_variables: MMECG processed/loso fold_01 strict LOSO split
rpeak Gaussian target sigma=5 samples (25 ms)
success_criteria: Training completes on fold_01; oracle_anchor_ola_pcc sanity is high (~0.95+).
Anchor F1@100ms clearly improves over the ~0.3 predicted-anchor baseline (target 0.6-0.8).
predicted_anchor_ola_pcc rises well above the dense full-window floor (~0.40) toward the oracle ceiling as anchor F1 improves.
go_no_go: Goal is to prove anchor->continuous coupling, not to beat radarODE. If anchor F1 cannot improve, do not stack a waveform decoder; rethink the localization signal/representation.
failure_interpretation: If anchor F1 stays near baseline, WSST may lack the beat-timing signal at this resolution; revisit representation (SST/phase) or add temporal context before more modeling.
